::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 30th [1868]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 201-2
:::

My dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd)
Thanks for the [cheque](organizations/other_160.qmd) and for the proposal about the [Historical selections](cmy_books/cmybook_71.qmd). I am sending it on to [Miss Sewell](people/person_1301.qmd) to see whether she consents, it is what I myself should prefer, thinking joint accounts would be troublesome. The [Cameo](cmy_books/cmybook_73.qmd) looks exceedingly well and gives an uncommon appearance.[^1] I should like a copy to be sent to the [Dean of Chichester](people/person_709.qmd) and one to [Madame de Witt](people/person_423.qmd). To other friends I think it will not be necessary to send one.

I have had a MS lately to read by a [Miss Eyre](people/person_2008.qmd) who wishes me to write to you about it. It is called Gabrielle and her Guardians[^2] and strikes me as having a good deal of thought and promise, though there is a good deal of youth too. The hero is rather remarkably imagined, and the story catches the attention I found on reading it aloud

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: CMY appears to be referring to the illustration which Macmillan had had put on the title page.
[^2]: The book does not appear to have been published under this title, nor Miss Eyre to have published at this period under that name.
